The Siege of Terraven

After the victory over Prince Lukas at Oligoth, Ivar realized that the greatest threat against him was gone. Adrithyr had far more men, greater generals, and many great knights and mages, but none could rival the Bastard Prince. Using the power of Arkonil in his wicked crown, he was nigh unstoppable. Lukas was his one great hurdle, and he had hoped to make peace with the Prince, to ally with him and together remove their father from the throne to come to a somewhat peaceful resolution, but it seems Ivar abandoned that plan and decided killing was easier, or safer. 

Ivar nursed his wounds at Annevar, and made a declaration to the world as he gathered his forces. He would amass a great army, take control of the Lakefort (the most important strategic fortress in the north of Estor), and cross the Warming River. He was coming for Adrithyr. This threat was not taken lightly, Adrithyr chose to answer like a King, he holed up in his Castle in his walled city of Terraven, calling all his bannermen, Knights, and great Generals to a war council at his Palace. 

Notably he called Elena Syrell, the Mistress of Moonlight, and ruler of the Lakefort to his court. This decision puzzled his advisors and Lady Syrell, but she answered the call dutifully as a sword Knight of the realm. With all his generals and warriors at his side, Adrithyr decided on a battle strategy, no battle at all. He held all his forces in the city and simply waited for Ivar. Cowardice the people called it, never within earshot of the Royal army, but it was whispered in ears from the highborn lords to the lowest peasants. 

Ivar campaigned across the river almost completely uncontested, and found himself at the gates of Terraven within months. He took the Lakefort, burned the fields of White Plains, and began a siege on the city. 

There have been many sieges in Estor’s history, given that it is a land of Kings and Castles, but this is by far the bloodiest in history. Ivar laid siege to the city for 6 months, along with his fully amassed army of five thousand men. The siege was brutal, but not as bloody as it could have been. Ivar could likely have shattered the walls himself, but it seemed he hesitated to take the form of Arkonil until he needed to. The casualties from actual combat were low, Adrithyr sent barely one legion out of the walls to fight, and over the 6 months arrows were used sparingly, so barely a thousand soldiers actually died outside the initial clash on the walls.

The real brutality of this siege was within the walls. The worst part of the siege was hunger. Terraven is built on top of a large river, and has access to the sea, water and fish were in decent supply, but after the first month Ivar sent his few ships to hunt and pirate any fisherman who dared to attempt it. The people had plenty of water, but food became scarce quickly. That’s what they don’t tell you about a siege. When the rich get hungry they pull from the royal stores. When the poor get hungry they eat the grain, then they eat the livestock, then they eat their pets, and then they eat each other. Riots and thievery were rife in the city, and the great defending army had to institute martial law and became essentially a glorified police force. 

It seemed the city wouldn’t last another day, the people had started a riot and were parading toward the royal palace. Ivar had launched an attack against the west gate, using battering rams and ladders to assail the walls, all seemed lost. Then, as if from the mist and fog itself, an army appeared. Wearing fine steel armor and cloaks of gold, led by a mysterious golden clad knight, Ivar was attacked from his flank. 

As if it was planned, and risen from the grave himself, Prince Lukas was seen leading three royal legions from the west gate as Ivar turned to address his unknown attackers. He was trapped between the now rallied city with their thought to be dead prince, and an entirely new army in the fields beyond. 

We know now that the golden warriors were the Swords of Dawn, an army from the far west, beyond Konduell, led by the Champion of Shao Daraan, Prince Augustus of Lazarus. 

This was Ivar’s moment, and realization that he was not invincible. He took the form of Arkonil and beat back the royal army, but not the Prince. Lukas had been reborn in the storm he once wielded. His entire lower half was constructed of blue electricity, and he flew through the sky like a storm cloud, free from the tether of the earth. Lukas alongside Augustus, battled Ivar. They fought bravely, Ivar’s demonic blade couldn’t seem to catch Lukas as he flew, and it seemed to simply phase through Augustus entirely. Lukas called forth a great storm and a bolt of lightning struck Arkonil, forcing him to one knee, where Augustus stabbed through his left arm, wounding the foul demon. For the first time since he had taken up the Wicked Crown, Ivar was wounded, and forced to retreat.

The siege was ended, and the armies of Adrithyr and the two princes were victorious. Ivar snaked his way back across the river, abandoning all his newly taken lands and castles, and hid away within his fortress of Obelask. He has not been seen or heard from since. Some (including Adrithyr and his court) believe Ivar died of his wounds. Augustus disagrees.
